markets.question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

eventMetadata.context_description: In the early stages of the 2028 presidential cycle, trader consensus reflects substantial uncertainty with JD Vance holding the narrowest lead amid a fragmented field. Post-2024 election positioning, including vice-presidential visibility and party infrastructure advantages, supports Vance's standing, while Democratic options like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez draw from progressive donor and activist networks. Republican names such as Marco Rubio benefit from Senate and potential executive-branch experience that could translate into early endorsements. The compressed spread among top contenders stems from the absence of declared candidates, limited polling data, and open questions about 2026 midterm results that will shape party momentum and fundraising. Upcoming developments including primary filing deadlines, debate performances, and shifts in congressional leadership could widen gaps by clarifying viable paths through swing-state coalitions and Electoral College math.
